explicit_validation.explanation: Both LLM and human evaluations were conducted but human evaluation served only for dataset validation (ensuring plausibility and factual consistency of NegHalu examples), while LLM evaluation was used for model performance assessment on hallucination detection tasks; there is no comparison between LLM and human judgments on the same instances or metrics of agreement.

prompts.notes: Table shows the prompt template used in Round 2 verification by GPT-4 models. The prompt asks evaluators to judge based on two binary criteria: Logical Negation (whether negated text logically transforms meaning) and New Label Validity (whether hallucination label is correctly assigned). Examples of successful and failed cases are provided in the qualitative analysis.

guidelines.notes: Guidelines are described briefly: human evaluation aimed to 'ensure overall plausibility and factual consistency' and 'prevent inclusion of nonsensical or factually incorrect content.' Specific criteria mentioned include plausibility, factual consistency, and alignment with real-world knowledge. Examples of annotated cases are provided in qualitative analysis.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM evaluation criteria are specific to verifying dataset quality (logical transformation and label correctness), while human evaluation criteria focus on overall quality and factual soundness of the dataset. No overlapping criteria were evaluated by both methods.
